problems.title: Full objective does not identify relative semantic orientation
problems.evidence: ZY->-ZY leaves RE,LMA,LIA exactly invariant; I2 versus -I2 gives zero alignment losses and ridge MAE0.5 versus1.5
problems.assumptions: Real-valued embeddings, linear unnormalized attention as written; no final positivity restriction; fixed source predictor
problems.counterevidence: Useful empirical orientation can arise from optimization biases; no claim all published runs fail
problems.impact: Defeats general inference from optimized losses to compatible semantic coordinates, not reported empirical means
problems.repair: Add justified orientation-identifying constraints or narrow empirical claim and disclose ambiguity
problems.repair_verification: Exact algebra and independent finite calculations; no repaired model rerun

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read physical pp.3-6 Definition 2.3 and Eqs.(2)-(13). The graph encoder is linear-valued at its output, cities have independently learned encoders, and Eq.(11) uses unnormalized linear query/key products, without softmax or a nonnegative-output constraint.
independent_check.decisive_check: Fix ZX,A,Wq,Wk and reverse only ZY. Its mobility Gram matrix is unchanged. First anchor relative rows reverse sign but their normalized Gram matrix and second normalization do not change. Each cross-city matrix reverses sign, so both cycle products and intra-city targets in Eq.(12) are unchanged. This proves equality of the entire Eq.(13) objective for all weights and anchor draws. For ZX=I2,ZY=+/-I2,Wq=Wk=2^(1/4)I2, both alignment losses are zero. Centered ridge with alpha=1, source labels (1,3) gives beta=(-.5,.5),intercept=2; target predictions become (1.5,2.5) or (2.5,1.5), and MAE .5 or1.5.
independent_check.admissibility_detail: The theoretical GAT output permits an exact sign change: negate final value W and the corresponding source/destination blocks of its attention vector so pre-LeakyReLU scores stay unchanged, leaving the edge-score block fixed. Separate target parameters allow this without changing source predictions. Thus this is not merely an impossible output assignment or a simultaneous global coordinate rotation.
independent_check.counterevidence: Useful orientations can occur from optimization bias or additional constraints, and the result does not prove failure of every published fit. The later release uses affine query/key layers, so invariance is asserted for the written linear Eq.(11), not all affine source configurations. More common anchors cannot break the proved paper-objective sign symmetry.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major retained for the central inference in Definition 2.3 and Section3.4 that optimized losses ensure directly reusable semantic coordinates. An orientation-identifying cross-city condition or a narrower empirical claim is needed. No label-calibrated repair, saved-embedding diagnostic or rerun was performed.

problems.title: Released losses change targets and relative weighting
problems.location: Model/CoRE.py cross_align and cross_rec vs Eqs8-12
problems.evidence: Projected targets collapse with zero query/key maps; omitted second normalization; row-distance means differ from entry means
problems.assumptions: Current pinned release; standard pairwise epsilon accounted for
problems.counterevidence: Original source version and experiment configuration unknown; no observed optimization collapse
problems.impact: Current implementation is not the displayed objective; historical empirical impact unresolved
problems.repair: Reconcile actual objective, normalization and experiment version
problems.repair_verification: Static reading and independent matrix examples only

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Statically inspected Model/CoRE.py:64-100 against written Eqs.(8)-(12). Differences are version-specific; the 2025-11-07 release is not authenticated as the proceedings experiment code.
independent_check.decisive_check: At zero query/key weights and biases, release projected targets s_attn,t_attn and cycle matrices all vanish for arbitrary embeddings. The default pairwise-distance epsilon creates only the row-size numerical floor; with two rows in each city it is 4e-12. Written raw-Gram targets at ZX=ZY=I2 give .5+.5=1 in Eq.(12). cross_align normalizes sim rows once but not the Gram rows, contrary to text after Eq.(8). Mean squared row distances equals 1/N sum_ij error^2, not 1/N^2 sum_ij error^2, so scaling differs by matrix size and across loss terms.
independent_check.counterevidence: Code 1-Gram constants cancel in differences and are not defects themselves. data/get_dataset.py globally normalizes mobility counts, agreeing with averaged trips; no false missing-mobility-normalization issue retained. Permitted zero projections show a source objective degeneracy but do not demonstrate actual training collapse.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor release/objective mismatch, empirical historical influence Needs Evidence. Reconcile projected versus raw targets, both normalizations, dimension factors and weights with exact run versions before claiming reproduction; no complete implementation repair tested.

problems.title: Zero-label MAPE mask is applied after undefined division
problems.evidence: Labels[0,2], predictions[0,2.2] give NaN; pre-subset ratio gives0.1
problems.assumptions: At least one zero target; actual target arrays not inspected
problems.counterevidence: Strictly positive target arrays avoid the defect
problems.impact: Conditional metric failure; occurrence in paper unknown
problems.repair: Subset valid targets before division, define empty subset
problems.repair_verification: Independent arithmetic case passed; no author code changed

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read evaluator_cross_city.py:34-38 MAPE and metrics_local. The defect requires at least one zero label; excluded raw targets were not inspected.
independent_check.decisive_check: For labels(0,2),predictions(0,2.2), the first ratio is 0/0 and multiplying that NaN by a zero mask leaves NaN. The nonzero-subset calculation is abs(2.2-2)/2=.1; summing the original loss remains NaN. A nonzero prediction over zero label similarly gives infinity*0.
independent_check.counterevidence: Strictly positive targets bypass the defect; the example does not establish occurrence in any reported target array. Clipping negative predictions before scoring does not prevent 0/0 for a zero target.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor conditional metric bug. Select nonzero labels before dividing and explicitly define the empty-valid-subset policy; code edit and historical score recomputation remain unperformed.

checked_claims: Two-region exact zero alignment losses and ridge prediction difference
repair_verification: Exact objective invariance and ridge counterexample independently derived; no orientation-identifying replacement model verified. Projection/normalization discrepancies and zero-label arithmetic checked; implementation fixes not executed.
